app.title: MATERIA Workbench: crystal and magnetic structure refinement
app.summary: A person loads a starting crystal structure, a measured diffraction pattern and the instrument's parameters, or opens a bundled demo. The observed, calculated and difference curves are drawn with the reflection positions marked. The person drags handles to set the fit range, then frees or fixes grouped model parameters and runs a refinement, either all at once or staged. They read the agreement factors, the diagnostics, a validation verdict and the history of each step, and can undo any step. They can go on to a magnetic step that searches the leftover peaks for a propagation vector and ranks candidate magnetic groups by how well they fit. Finally they export the refined structure, a report and cross-check bundles for established refinement programs.

task.text: Fit a crystal (and optionally magnetic) structure model to measured diffraction data by least squares, and check and report the refined parameters with their uncertainties.

data.text: A structure model with a unit cell, space group and atomic sites; a measured diffraction pattern (intensity against time-of-flight, angle or d) or a list of single-crystal reflections or a pair distribution function; instrument calibration constants; and a table of refinable parameters with values and esds.
data.item: a refinable model parameter (cell length, site position, thermal parameter, profile term) fitted against one measured pattern

stage.text: refining a structure model against measured diffraction data, after collection and before reporting

mechanism.text: A pattern plot of observed, calculated and difference curves with draggable fit-range handles sits beside a grouped parameter table, where each row can be freed or fixed and edited in place. Refining updates the curves, esds and agreement factors, and each step goes into an undoable history. Tabs switch to a validation dashboard, a 3D model and a posterior view, and a magnetic step and an assistant drawer act on the same session.

field.text: Rietveld, single-crystal and PDF structure refinement in crystallography

workflow.name: fit a parametric model to measured data and check the fit

steps.here: Load CIF, Load data and Load instrument cards, with format auto-detection, or pick a bundled demo; each card shows what was parsed

steps.step: choose the range of data the model is fitted to
steps.here: drag blue handles on the obs/calc/diff plot to set the fit window; switch the axis between TOF, d and Q, zoom with Shift-drag or scroll, and hover for a readout

steps.step: choose which model parameters are free and set their starting values
steps.here: grouped parameter table (scale, background, lattice, profile, ADPs, positions, occupancy) with a free/fixed toggle per row or group and editable values

steps.step: compute a value from the data
steps.here: Refine runs least squares on the free set; a staged mode frees scale, background, cell, profile, ADPs and positions in turn; esds, wR and diagnostics notes update
Validation tab gives a verdict, agreement factors, normalized residuals, cumulative χ², the worst peaks and convergence, with actions that point to the fix
each refine, tie or edit is a named step in a history that can be stepped back or forward, and the history is saved with the project
export the refined CIF, a report, CSV, a project JSON, and GSAS-II, FullProf or PDFgui bundles to cross-check the fit

distinctive: every parameter is constrained by space-group symmetry, and refined values carry esds
instrument and thermal parameters may not be refined together; the person alternates between the groups until neither moves
a magnetic step takes the peaks the nuclear fit leaves unexplained, searches them for a propagation vector and ranks candidate magnetic groups by fit
exports are bundles for established programs, so the same fit can be rerun and checked there
an optional assistant proposes each change through an approval card, and every change it makes can be undone
